steps.autolyseDesc: Mix flours: [{{flours}}] and {{water}}g of lukewarm water. Cover the bowl.
steps.fridgeDesc: Work in {{yeast}}g of yeast and salt. Put the bowl straight into the fridge (4 °C){{work}}
steps.fridgeWork: and you can head to work!
steps.bathDesc: Take the dough out of the fridge. Submerge the bowl in lukewarm water (30-32 °C) to warm it up after the whole day.
steps.mixDesc: Knead the dough thoroughly ({{hydration}}% hydration, {{mins}} min - {{method}}). At {{protein}}g protein the dough is nicely elastic.
steps.mixMorningDesc: Knead the dough {{mins}} min ({{method}}) and get ready for folding.
steps.foldDesc: {{count}} rounds of 4 stretch & folds from the sides (~{{gap}} min apart) to strengthen the gluten network.
steps.foldMorningDesc: {{count}} quick folds from all 4 sides (~{{gap}} min apart).
steps.shapeDesc: Shape the loaf and place it in the banneton (~{{mins}} min proofing at {{temp}}°C).
steps.preheatDesc: Turn the oven on full with the Dutch oven inside.
steps.doneDesc: Take the bread out and let it cool completely on a rack.
steps.incorpEveningDesc: Work {{yeast}}g yeast, 10g salt, {{honey}}g honey and {{fat}}g butter/oil into the autolyse (dissolve honey in 20ml lukewarm water).
steps.foldEveningDesc: One set of folds from all sides, no kneading.
steps.shapeEveningDesc: Preshape, rest 5 minutes and give the loaf its final shape. The dough should rise by roughly {{rise}} % in the bowl – warmer dough finishes bulking sooner, the fridge completes the rest.
steps.fridgeEveningDesc: Place dough in banneton and refrigerate (4-6 °C) overnight.
steps.bakeStartDesc: Score the cold dough straight from the fridge and place in the hot pot. Bake 20 min covered at 245 °C.
steps.bakeUncoverDesc: Remove the lid and lower temperature to 210 °C. Bake 15 minutes.
steps.doorAjarDesc: Leave the oven door slightly open for the last 5 minutes for a thin crispy crust.
steps.doneEveningDesc: Take the bread out and cool for at least 1 hour on a rack.
steps.yudaneDesc: Pour {{water}} g boiling water over {{flour}} g flour, stir into a thick gel and let it cool (ideally the day before, refrigerated). Add to the main dough at mixing.

ferm.advice_over: Over-proofing risk – reduce yeast, shorten the time or lower the temperature.
ferm.advice_severely-over: Severe over-proofing risk – cut the yeast significantly or shorten fermentation.
ferm.advice_under: The dough will likely under-proof – consider more yeast, a warmer spot or more time.
ferm.hint: Model: yeast rate by temperature (table peaking at ~32–36 °C, ~12 % in the fridge), effects of salt, sugar/honey, fat, hydration and flour type; sourdough has slower dynamics. NH24 = normalized hours at 24 °C – total fermentation work as hours of proofing at 24 °C. Maturity index ~100 % = ideally proofed dough (below 85 % under-proofed, above 115 % over-proofed); the target is calibrated per schedule and your times and temperatures. Fridge cooling follows a measured curve (The Sourdough Journey: 25.6 °C -> ~10 °C in 3 h, ~4.4 °C in 7.5 h) and in fridge modes the maturity target is adjusted by dough temperature (27 °C -> ~30 % rise, 24 °C -> ~50 %, 21 °C -> ~75 %, 18 °C -> ~100 %).
